Thanks for opening a pull request :slightly_smiling_face: 

Feature pull requests should be associated to a *feature proposal* to justify the need for implementing the feature in Godot core. Please open a proposal on the [Godot proposals](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals) repository (and link to this pull request in the proposal's body).

Please separate your enhancements into different pull requests and attach Godot improvement proposals.

Edited: There is code changes here that is unrelated to Animation Tweaks.

I merged godotengine/godot/master into iceball457/godot/animation-tweaks on accident and then reverted it. There are no extraneous differences between iceball457/godot/animation-tweaks and godotengine/godot/master as of commit f418603522ebda0e00dd1e39646ceb42b8b62055 ("Merge pull request #102749 from timothyqiu/tree-buttons-offset ... Fix TreeItem button tooltip trigger area offset") at the time this branch was forked.

@fire Let me know if I should merge master back into my branch, I don't know if that could make the code review easier now that my branch is all sloppy. In the meantime, I'll make a feature proposal

These code changes have nothing to do with animation.

- `core/os`
- `doc/classes/TileMap`
- `platform/ios`
- `scene/gui`
- `servers/rendering/renderer_rd`
- `scene/2d/line_2d`
- Parts of `doc/classes`

Those changes come from commit d070530275ae2137f67770fcbd0694e1d9fd8e79. I don't know why changes in 04d7fd2519f6bd31ae13d9b60353224d085633d0 result in "This merge commit was added into this branch cleanly", but I do see that the sum of the merge and revert show diffs even though the actual files are identical.

What I need to know is if I should close this PR and re-open it with a fresh branch.

Edit: I may also want to split this PR into "Animation Tree State Machine Teleport Blending" and "Animation Player Force Restart Animation", as the two changes aren't strictly mutual.

> What I need to know is if I should close this PR and re-open it with a fresh branch.

There's never a need to close / re-open PRs, you can fix things and force-push to the existing branch :slightly_smiling_face: 
(force-pushing is done with `git push --force-with-lease`, **don't** use `-f` or `--force`)

In this case, you'd need to get rid of all the commits not related to your changes. There are different ways, here two possible options:
1. `git rebase -i master`, mark everything that's not yours as "skip"

1. `git tag bkup` (to save current status; alternatively keep it remote)
    `git reset --hard master`
    `git cherry-pick <all revision hashes that you want to keep>`
Here's the feature proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11769

A quote from the feature proposal

> It should be able to determine the teleport and use it, but a quick look at the code shows that this does not appear to be the case.

The code does not need to know that it is teleporting, it was programmed to reuse as much transition code as possible. All we actually care about is which animation node is next and which transition we are going to use to get there. In the case of resetting a state machine to start, the transition is already skipped due to the internals of _set_current. A "force_instant" parameter might be necessary though (force a transition with 0 duration).

> My feeling is that the correct way is doing what you are trying to do [over there] in this block.

Let's suppose we remove the teleport_transition information from the _find_next function. Now, we need to manage the case where our return value is null, as some pairs of nodes in the state machine have no transition, and we won't be injecting the teleport_transition information until later. (We wouldn't previously have had to deal with the null case, as this method was previously only accessible in a travel case: the teleport cases get pruned off before this point in master.)

Now, we have to decide where to re-add the missing transition info.

There are two options, we either need to set a non-null value for this NextInfo struct before every subsequent usage of _find_next's return value; or we need to pass a null case all the way back up to _process so we can manage re-adding the now missing transition information in the teleport block as you request.

Now, there is only one usage of _next_info, so treating the null case immediately before the return value's usage would take less keystrokes than this paragraph; however, the next usage of the return value is on the very next line of code, so I see no value in treating a null case when we could have simply not returned null in the first place (we even already have access to the state machine as a dependency injection in _find_next, since we are using other values as well).

As for passing a null case back to _process? _transition_to_next_recursive is the only function with _find_next in its children that gets called from _process. It is a recursive function, so in order to properly emulate the current behavior, we would need to create another recursive function that does most of what _transition_to_next_recursive already does.

> So what should be done here is that when a transition_request is received, if there is already fading, it is discarded and replaced with a new teleport_transition.

We never want to discard fading, as fading is not discarded for normal travels either. We want to queue the transition after the current transition (but not at the end of the current path, to best match the behavior of explicitly defined transitions). No matter if the current transition is a travel or a teleport; and no matter if the queued transition is a travel, a series of travels, or a teleport, we want the same blending behavior. To that end, all transition requests that can't be fulfilled using explicitly defined transitions are replaced with a direct transition to the destination node, then fed into the same pipeline.

> By the way, if your intention in removing them is for perfect smoothing, then this implementation is not sufficient.

I only know that the behavior is correct from experimentation [custom_build_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18814762/custom_build_test.zip). I tried two things, simply pushing the next teleport state onto the next_state_queue, and clearing the queue before pushing the teleport target as a solo element in the state machine's path.

If you don't clear the path before adding the next destination, it's possible to chain a bunch of teleports one after another. This is actually my preferred behavior; however, I am trying to replicate the behavior of an explicitly defined transition. The following snippet has identical behavior when compared to a densely connected state machine. More specifically, the behavior of an isolated node is identical to any node receiving connections from every other node. (Although the teleport transition has a lower priority (as intended).)

> I would actually prefer if the teleport_transition is appended to the end of the transition queue. In much the same way that explicitly defined transitions are already queued.

Okay, I understand what you want to do and it makes sense to implement it.

However, I remember that the current teleport has the behavior of discarding the current state and moving to the specified state. So this change causes a rather large compatibility breakdown. We cannot approve that. I also believe that there is a certain demand for the behavior of discarding the current state/transition.

So, if you want to wait for the transition to end without destroying it, I think you need to make that an optional argument as follows:

```
void teleport(String p_state, bool p_immediate = true) {
  teleport_request  = p_immediate ? TELEPORT_REQUEST_IMMEDIATE : TELEPORT_REQUEST_WAIT_CURRENT_TRANSITION;
```

This may make the teleport_request flag should be enum like this:

```
enum TeleportRequest {
  TELEPORT_REQUEST_NONE,
  TELEPORT_REQUEST_IMMEDIATE,
  TELEPORT_REQUEST_WAIT_CURRENT_TRANSITION,
};
```

> The code does not need to know that it is teleporting, it was programmed to reuse as much transition code as possible. All we actually care about is which animation node is next and which transition we are going to use to get there. In the case of resetting a state machine to start, the transition is already skipped due to the internals of _set_current. A "force_instant" parameter might be necessary though (force a transition with 0 duration).

This is a suggestion from a code readability point of view. I don't recommend writing in such a way that teleport_transition may be used even though teleport is not indicated. Even if it is safe in your PR, if someone modify the state machine in the future, the teleport_transition could be used in an unintended case.

As indicated above, you should only do this in certain blocks when `p_immediate` is `false` (`teleport_request` flag is `TELEPORT_REQUEST_WAIT_CURRENT_TRANSITION`).

From what I'm understanding, there needs to be a distinction between "teleporting" (which will skip over in-progress blending) and "jumping" (which queues the same as any other travel move).

May I suggest:
enum TeleportRequest {
  TELEPORT_REQUEST_NONE,
  TELEPORT_REQUEST_IMMEDIATE,
  TELEPORT_REQUEST_QUEUE,
};

Let's imagine a teleport request and a jump request happen on the same frame. Jump requests aren't anything special, and we would expect a teleport request to override all current animations and immediately start the requested animation. I think `TELEPORT_REQUEST_QUEUE` can be a `bool jump_request`, so that we can handle teleport request first inside _process and set both `teleport_request` and `jump_request` to false before the jump request is handled. This would prevent script order from having an effect on the behavior of a state machine, but it would also prevent intentional overriding of a teleport request. At a glance, I think this is a good trade-off?

On the API side, Instead of replacing the current teleport behavior:

Option one:

Add the p_immediate flag to playback travel, and add a new teleport method. This method adds the least amount of vocabulary for the user, as it barely distinguishes between a jump and a teleport. However, the p_reset_on_teleport and p_reset arguments will not be used for non-immediate transitions, as that information is defined in the transition.

[change] `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback::travel(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset_on_teleport, bool p_immediate)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback::teleport(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset, bool p_immediate)`

Option two:

Leave the current teleport behavior as is. Expose new travel_smooth, teleport, and jump calls to the user. This will require a vocabulary addition, I do actually think `default_transition` is the correct name for the behavior I am attempting to implement, but I am open to `jump_transition` or leaving it as teleport_transition (iff we name the jump function something like `teleport_smooth`)

[keep] `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback::travel(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset_on_teleport)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachingPlayback::travel_smooth(const StringName &p_state)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachingPlayback::teleport(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachingPlayback::jump(const StringName &p_state)`

EDIT: Option three:

Leave the current teleport behavior as is. Expose new travel_smooth, teleport, and jump calls to the user. Remove the teleport transition field and have the user pass in their own transitions.

[keep] `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback::travel(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset_on_teleport)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachingPlayback::travel_smooth(const StringName &p_state, AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition p_transition)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachingPlayback::teleport(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset)`
[add] `AnimationNodeStateMachingPlayback::jump(const StringName &p_state, AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition p_transition)`

> This means that teleport_transition is not available between states that are connected.

In both of the suggested API changes, teleport_transition was made available to states that had a valid path by calling something like `myTree.jump("state_name")`.

`travel`  would be "Attempt to follow a path. Teleport to the requested state if there is no path." (Current behavior)
`travel_smooth` would be "Attempt to follow a path. Use `default_transition` if there is no path." (Behavior of 'travel' in my original commit.)
`teleport` would be "Drop *everything* and play the requested state immediately." (Not available to the user. Used in start().)
`jump` would be "Use `default_transition` to move to the requested state." (New behavior)

> I thought about using the term queue too like teleport(String p_state, bool p_queue), but I think there is a concern about teleport between states with paths if you put the travel path and teleport requests in the same queue.

I am not intending to put any teleports into the same queue as transitions. Whenever a teleport is requested, we should clear the queue, stop the current transition, and immediately play the requested state. This is to match the current behavior of a teleport request.

> So what you are trying to do now is say that both of the following states are handled equally and they cannot use teleport_transition.
>
>   queue[A(travel), B(travel), C(travel)]
>  queue[A(travel), B(teleport), C(teleport)]

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aff23b0c-2c23-4d5b-833d-e8f9f707d7be)

Let's suppose, on master, we have a script (I use c#) that requests a bunch of travels:

```cs
// we start at "shake 2" //mtTree.Teleport("shake 2")
myTree.Travel("shake 3")
myTree.Travel("circle 3")
```

The resulting state of the machine is as follows:
path: `{ "circle", "circle 3" }`, current: `"circle 2"`, and we are transitioning from "shake 2" and have a bunch of information about that transition.

Note that even though we traveled to "shake 3", we don't actually see it in the travel queue. The current implementation uses a queue to remember what steps it needs to take, not to allow the user to queue an arbitrary series of steps. All previous entries in the travel queue are nuked and replaced with a new A* path.

Over on this theoretical commit, we might have:

```cs
// we start at "shake 2" //mtTree.Teleport("shake 2")
myTree.Teleport("shake 3")
myTree.Teleport("circle 3")
```

Teleports are not transitions, so they cannot be queued. Nor would queuing teleports be useful, as they have 0 duration. The resulting state of the machine should be:

path: `{ }`, current: `"circle 3"`, and NO active transitions. The current transition, if any, should be cleared by the end of the frame.

I think it is not practical to implement `travel_smooth()` and `jump()`. The reason is that it is not safe to use a resource object `AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition` as an argument with AnimationTree; We should prevent the currently processing BlendTree to be able to reference the AnimationNodeTransition and any other resource held by an external BlendTree to avoid pointer confusion, it is why the StateMachine uses the name string managed by the StateMachine rather than `AnimationNode` resource to specify the state.

Also, as I mentioned above, I think immediate teleport is equivalent to `start()`.

So in the end I proposed the following:

> However, there is a concern that the above would make teleport only too sophisticated and make travel() unnecessary.

> So, for the sake of generalization, I have come up with the following method. How about it?
> - The transition name is default_transition
> - Add queue(String p_state)
>   - Add p_state to the travel_path array. If there is no connection, default_transition is used.
> - Add queue_travel(String p_state)
>   - Concatenates the A* path from the last element of the travel_path array to p_state. If travel_path is empty, it is equivalent to travel().

I think using `default_transition` when it is queued and has no connection would satisfy what you want to implement. If there is no insufficiency there for you, I think this is the simplest way with the fewest API additions and keeping compatibility.

I suppose there are GUI concerns about putting everything in the `travel_path`, but I think there is no problem unless you add a mode to use queue on the Editor.

Also, by using the same queue for travel and non-connected moving, the user can see from the `get_travel_path()` what user has added just before which might uses `default_transition`. If you want to override that, you may want to add more APIs (like `remove_at_travel_path()`, `insert_travel_path()`, etc.) to edit the `travel_path`.

The reason for preventing `travel_path` editing so far has been to prevent to collapse transitions due to the inability to handle unconnected transitions, but if this PR's purpose is to handle that, then it should be able to support it. Considering them, I think the title of this proposal/PR could be just "Add a `default_transition` for unconnected state transitions and allow `travel_path` to include unconnected states".

> I think it is not practical to implement travel_smooth() and jump(). The reason is that it is not safe to use a resource object AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition as an argument with AnimationTree

I can implement them using default_transition, instead of passing around resources willy-nilly.

> I think using default_transition when it is queued and has no connection would satisfy what you want to implement. If there is no insufficiency there for you, I think this is the simplest way with the fewest API additions and keeping compatibility.

Yes, if option 3 is insufficient or dangerous, option 2 is what you have described here. Personally, I think option three was the worst one anyway and was only even suggested for completeness.

> The reason for preventing travel_path editing so far has been to prevent to collapse transitions due to the inability to handle unconnected transitions, but if this PR's purpose is to handle that, then it should be able to support it. Considering them, I think the title of this proposal/PR could be just "Add a default_transition for unconnected state transitions and allow travel_path to include unconnected states".

That is the best way to look at it. I really don't intend to give the user access to the travel path. I am not opposed to it, but it is a task for another PR, and another feature proposal.

Edit: My original intention would have been "Add fallback 'default_transition', for discontinuous travel requests."

Edit (regarding the proposed queue-ing strategy):

> So, for the sake of generalization, I have come up with the following method. How about it?
> 
>     * The transition name is default_transition
> 
>     * Add queue(String p_state)
>       
>       * Add p_state to the travel_path array. If there is no connection, default_transition is used.
> 
>     * Add queue_travel(String p_state)
>       
>       * Concatenates the A* path from the last element of the travel_path array to p_state. If travel_path is empty, it is equivalent to travel().

This feature proposal wasn't intended to modify the way travel requests are assessed; however, if this functionality is desired, I am already in the mindset to make such an addition. This would come in addition to general changes to non-teleport default transitions, as opposed to replacing them, to prevent losing features that I need in my own projects. 

All that being said, I will try to reconcile our discussion into a commit sometime this week.

@TokageItLab I have completely severed the definitions of teleporting and jumping.

- The internals of the class are still able to teleport using exactly the same code as before.
- The user facing `teleport_request`s from `travel` have been accompanied by a `jump_request` which uses the supplied `default_transition`. A jump is only requested if a user specified travel has no valid path, or if the user specifically requests a jump.
- The user is now able to specify an optional `force_jump` flag that skips the path-finding and resolves https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98617#issuecomment-2464858233. 

Unfortunately, it took me an hour longer than expected because I accidentally synced my changes instead of forcing a push... :(

I have two concerns about the code as of the time of writing this:

1. The user-facing `p_reset_on_teleport` might be redundant, as I don't think the user can *force* a teleport anymore. It's still necessary on the internal version of _travel_main, but might not need to be exposed.
2. I still don't know what to do about [line 1073](https://github.com/Iceball457/godot/blob/a5bd0d7678ebf5616e880051b672ebf795e52ccb/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp#L1073). The build system claims that the overloaded operator is invalid or something like that.

Edit: More info about the failed build tests (from the previous commit that they ran on):

```
scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp:1058:60: error: use of deleted function 'bool Ref<T>::operator==(std::nullptr_t) const [with T = AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition; std::nullptr_t = std::nullptr_t]'
 1058 |                 if (p_state_machine->default_transition == nullptr) {
      |                                                            ^~~~~~~
In file included from ./core/math/expression.h:34,
                 from scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.h:34,
                 from scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp:31:
./core/object/ref_counted.h:97:14: note: declared here
   97 |         bool operator==(std::nullptr_t) const = delete;
      |              ^~~~~~~~
scons: *** [scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.linuxbsd.template_debug.x86_64.o] Error 1
scons: building terminated because of errors.
INFO: Time elapsed: 00:00:39.52 
Error: Process completed with exit code 2.
```

> I still don't know what to do about [line 1073](https://github.com/Iceball457/godot/blob/a5bd0d7678ebf5616e880051b672ebf795e52ccb/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp#L1073). The build system claims that the overloaded operator is invalid or something like that.

Isn't default transition `Ref<Resource>`? Then it should be `p_state_machine->default_transition.is_null()` since `Ref.ptr` can be `nullptr` but `Ref` isn't.

Although parameters were removed from the user facing API, they are still accessible internally. Every case that previously resulted in a teleport still results in a teleport EXCEPT for when the user requests a non-connected state with the travel command, which is now processed via `default_transition`. Because the user can no longer force a teleport via `travel`, there is no need to specify what to do when a teleport is triggered.

That being said, I don't find it hard to imagine users wishing to manually trigger a teleport for one reason or another. It would be possible to allow the user to request a teleport with a `teleport(StringName state, bool reset_animation)`. Users are currently only able to get teleports via `start` in this commit (not very flexible).
@AThousandShips Is the "breaks compat" a tag that I should try and fix? Or is it more of a "wait until the next version number to consider this PR" kinda deal
It's something to discuss, you've changed the parameters of an exposed method which breaks compatibility

The parameter would no longer do anything. The removed parameter is `p_reset_on_teleport`, but the whole point of this PR is preventing the need to teleport inside a travel request.

It could be left as a vestigial parameter without any additional work on my end; however, I think it's best to leave this change for later unless there are other teams who desperately need this change.

It still breaks compatibility and needs to be handled, you will need to register compatibility methods, see [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/handling_compatibility_breakages.html) for instructions
In my opinion, p_reset_on_teleport is still needed as commented in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102784#discussion_r1958782413 and compatibility is not broken.

To be clear, I did not modify `_travel_main`, which still *needs* that parameter to pass to `start`. I *did* modify the parameters of `travel` whose only job is to pass the parameters of the exposed method into the private method. However, in the context of a user-requested travel, the branch of code that `reset_on_teleport` is checked in cannot be reached. For that reason, the parameter has no effect from the user's perspective.

Edit: I reviewed again, the branch actually can be reached if the user requests a travel while the state machine is sitting in the "/Start" state. This means the parameter is like 99% useless, but not vestigial.

Edit 2: Further inspection reveals that the branch that `reset_request_on_teleport` used to be checked in now uses `p_state_machine->default_transition->is_reset()`.

For example, when state "N" and "A" are not connected and your current state is "N" (but "N"'s playback is end) with that "A"'s current time is `0.5`:

- start("A", true) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time `0.0`
- start("A", false) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time `0.5`
- travel("A", true) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time `0.0`
- travel("A", false) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time `0.5`
- queue("A") will use default_transition from "N" and playback "A" time is depend on the default_transition's Reset property
- queue_travel("A") will use default_transition from "N" and playback "A" time is depend on the default_transition's Reset property

Since the above 4 are existing behavior, you must keep them.

Well, if the specification that we are currently discussing and coming to terms with, it may not be necessary to distinguish Start and End from other States. Since it is only important whether they are connected or not.

Original behavior:

- start("A", true) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0
- start("A", false) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5
- travel("A", true) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0
- travel("A", false) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5
- queue is not implemented
- queue_travel is not implemented


Current behavior:

- start("A", true) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0
- start("A", false) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5
- travel("A", true) will clear the empty path then add "A" to the travel path
- travel("A", false) will clear the empty path then add "A" to the travel path
- queue("A") will add "A" to the end of the travel path
- queue_travel will add "A" to the end of the travel path

The behavior in the latest commit uses the default_transition *instead* of teleporting whenever no path is found. That was the premise of the PR, after all.
The user has NO access to manual teleports. I was concerned about this a while back, and proposed adding a public `teleport(state)` to re-introduce this behavior in case it was desired.

It is also possible for me to revert the changes to `travel` and re-implement the PR as an new public `travel_smooth` that uses the default transition instead of teleporting.

Edit: Accidentally called `start` "not-implemented", whoops

> Well, if the specification that we are currently discussing and coming to terms with, it may not be necessary to distinguish Start and End from other States. Since it is only important whether they are connected or not.

Start and end actually do work properly even without the special case I added for them.

The state machine for this example is ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"] connected in order. Playback is currently looping inside A (or at the end, whatever). All other states are waiting at 0.5.

> Since the above 4 are existing behavior, you must keep them.

Proposed behavior for the next commit (regarding compatibility):

start("E", true) will move to "E" immediately and playback "E" at time 0.0
start("E", false) will move to "E" immediately and playback "E" at time 0.5
travel("E", true) will clear the travel path then add ["B", "C", "D", "E"] to the travel path (valid connection found)
travel("E", false) will clear the travel path then add ["B", "C", "D", "E"] to the travel path (valid connection found)
travel_smooth("E") will clear the travel path then add ["B", "C", "D", "E"] to the travel path (valid connection found)
queue("E") will add "E" to the end of the travel path (it will end up using `default_transition`)
queue_travel("E") will add ["B", "C", "D", "E"] to the end of the travel path (valid connection found)

Now, we wait 10 seconds so that all the machines are at "E".

start("A", true) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0
start("A", false) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5
travel("A", true) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0 (no connection found)
travel("A", false) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5 (no connection found)
travel_smooth("A") will clear the travel path then add ["A"] to the travel path (no connection found)
queue("A") will add "A" to the end of the travel path
queue_travel("A") will add ["A"] to the end of the travel path (no connection found)

For the final example, let's imagine the player gave us an input while we were in the middle of `travel` in the first example. We are currently in state B. The travel path is ["C"]

start("A", true) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0
start("A", false) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5
travel("A", true) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0 (no connection found)
travel("A", false) will move to "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5 (no connection found)
travel_smooth("A") will clear the travel path then add ["A"] to the travel path (no connection found)
queue("A") will add "A" to the end of the travel path for a total of ["C", "A"]
queue("E") will add "E" to the end of the travel path for a total of ["C", "E"]
queue_travel("A") will find a path from the last entry in the travel path "C" to the requested "A" (it finds none and just queues "A") for total of ["C", "A"]
queue_travel("E") will find a path from the last entry in the travel path "C" to the requested "E" (it finds ["D", "E"]) for total of ["C", "D", "E"]

> Current behavior:
start("A", true) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.0
start("A", false) will move "A" immediately and playback "A" at time 0.5
travel("A", true) will clear the empty path then add "A" to the travel path
